done_when: A follow-up that names a period the app reads itself (anything the app's date reader parses, such as last 30 days, explicit dates and date ranges, plus a month with or without a year, a year, a quarter with or without a year, or last, previous or this month, quarter or year) answers for that period whatever window the model emits; fiscal and other wording (FY, YTD, next month, previous week) keeps the model's window and the period control; a question naming no period still inherits or aggregates as before, and an amount is never read as a year; changing an answer's period still re-runs on the chosen period

findings.body: `parseExplicitMonthYear` now runs before the app's existing `parseTimeWindow` reader, but its patterns match substrings inside richer date expressions. For example, “Show 2026-01-01 to 2026-07-09” matches `2026-01` and becomes January 2026 instead of the explicit date range; “Show Jan-Mar 2026” matches `Mar 2026` and becomes March instead of January–March. These are date forms the app reader already parses, so they must override the model with the complete parsed period. Run the general date reader before these substring helpers or prevent the helpers from matching inside dates and ranges.
findings.title: Not done: explicit dates and ranges can be truncated to one month

findings.body: The amount-range classifier recognizes only `actual` and `budget` as measure prefixes and omits `costs` and `expenses` from its quantity prefixes. Consequently, a follow-up such as “Show costs between 2024 and 2025” is classified as calendar years 2024–2025 and overrides the prior/model window, even though the same code treats an `Actual` range as an amount range. This violates the requirement that an amount is never read as a year. Apply the same amount vocabulary used by `COPULA_AMOUNT_PREFIX_PATTERN` to range classification.
findings.title: Not done: cost and expense amount ranges are treated as calendar years

findings.body: The new matrix calls `ChatService.ask` through `makeFixture`, whose model, query executor/database, audit service, dimensions, reports, and resolver are fakes. The period-control rerun test uses the same fixture. Repository scripts register only Node and jsdom/Vitest suites, with no Playwright user flow against a running API and real database. Thus the named-period override, inheritance/aggregation, amount protection, and control rerun remain proven only below the required end-to-end boundary; the successful close run does not supply the required browser proof.
findings.title: Not done: end-to-end Ask coverage for period selection and reruns

why: An Ask question that names a period, such as July 2026, answers for that period even as a follow-up in the same thread; the model's own window and the previous answer's window used to win
